relevance_note: The paper describes a Japanese family with Behçet's disease in which 'the heterozygous C243Y mutation was present in all familial patients with BD examined', with individual clinical histories for patients 1–6.
method_note: Read the whole paper (no tables; no supplementary section). Values were entered by hand from my reading into a Python script in my scratch directory, which built the JSON and checked every span verbatim against the paper. Labels: the paper's own labels in their most frequent form: 'patient 1', 'patient 2' and 'patient 6' occur mostly in lower case; 'Patient 3', 'Patient 4' and 'Patient 5' occur only capitalised. The proband's healthy younger brother (tested negative) has no own label and is 'younger brother of patient 1' (rule 2). The father is mentioned only through 'paternally derived (not investigated)' and gets no row. Variant rows: C243Y for patients 1–5 (patients 3–5 tied by 'all affected members, apart from patient 6' being sequenced and the mutation being 'present in all familial patients with BD examined'). Patient 6 was not sequenced and the brother lacks the mutation, so neither has a variant row. Patient 1 also has a second TNFAIP3 row for 'three nucleotide deletions in an intron of upper exon 3' (no notation printed; unclear whether one 3-nt deletion or three deletions; paternal origin not investigated). Notation: the paper prints 'C243Y' and '728 G>A' without 'p.'/'c.' prefixes and no transcript; recorded as printed, with no prefix added. The genomic string 'chr6_138197226_G>A' is recorded without a build: the methods mention alignment to GRCh37, but the paper does not tie the build to this coordinate. Inheritance left 'not reported' for all: the mother carries C243Y but the paper never states the proband inherited it from her. Uveitis/ocular inflammation excluded for patients 1–6 from the group statement 'None of the patients had exhibited ocular lesions of BD' (the six named family patients). Brother: 'neither BD symptoms' recorded as one excluded feature; his checklist items are left 'not reported' rather than inferred from 'BD symptoms'. Patient 1's perianal ulcer is not counted as a genital or gastrointestinal ulcer in the checklist. Lab values without the authors' interpretation (white cell count, neutrophil rate, haemoglobin, immunoglobulins) were not recorded as features; CRP is recorded as observed because the paper gives the normal range (<0.1 mg/dL) beside the value 0.27 mg/dL. HLA-B51 negativity not recorded (a genetic marker, not a feature). Contradictions: (1) The abstract says 'all affected family members carried a heterozygous C243Y mutation', but the Figure 1 legend says 'Sequence analysis was not possible on patient 6'; n_patients_reported is left null because the authors never state a count of carriers. (2) Patient 6 is said to have 'recurrent oral and genital ulcers', then 'A history of genital ulcers could not be ascertained'; the observed row is kept with that sentence in severity_or_detail and her checklist genital-ulcer item is 'not reported'. (3) The abstract says the 6 patients 'had suffered from frequent oral ulcers, genital ulcers and erythaema nodosum-like lesions', but patient 1's own history mentions no genital ulcers; the group statement was not used for individual features.
